description.narrative: Stakeholder Effects- Increased access to climate finance for Energy Efficient (EE) equipment by MSMEs: Through the Project, IFC will support PCPL in increasing access to climate finance for EE equipment by MSMEs. Most MSMEs in India are traditional and small and deploy inefficient technologies. The sizeable quantum of energy consumed by the MSME sector combined with the use of conventional and less efficient technologies offers a significant potential for energy savings through replacement of old machines with new EE machines and even through EE retrofits in the prevailing production processes. Assessment of Contribution to Market Creation- Competitiveness: The proposed investment is expected to promote greater competitiveness in the MSME climate finance market through demonstration and replication channels. Despite the prevalence of strong and mature FIs in India that have strong liquidity, green finance is still a relatively new concept for most private sector FIs in India, especially when the target segment is MSMEs, and more so for smaller NBFCs. IFCs support through the Project will demonstrate to other banks and NBFCs that there is a scalable business opportunity in this market segment and is expected to lead to replication from other FIs in the market, promoting greater competitiveness in the market with more banks and NBFCs scaling up financing in this segment.

The proposed investment envisages an Indian Rupee (INR) denominated investment of up to US$25 million equivalent in Profectus Capital Private Limited (PCPL, or the Company). The investment will be made by subscribing to green bonds issued by PCPL with a tenor of up to five years and the proceeds will be used for financing energy efficient (EE) machinery for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) (the Project).
